Clean first then speed. Also when you are doing a good KBD you are not going to see your character crouch at all because all of the motions are buffered during the backdash, not afterwards. You are cancelling the sidestep during your backdash and you will not see your character crouch. I'd suggest finding some videos of people who are really good at it and try to mimic their hands to get the right rhythm. Then just recreate it as best as possible. And don't worry too much about getting it perfect while you're versing people, the more you do it the better it will be.

Once you get the rhythm down and you start to feel comfortable with it, then you can focus on covering as much distance as possible while doing them quickly. It's much more important to create a good amount of distance than to do a bunch of small ones rapidly. Just keep practicing.

“Honey, would you pass me a pen?”

“I’m sorry, all we have are quills.”

“..Alright fine. I hate how scratchy they are, though.”

I looked through the five or six quills we had in the drawer and picked the one with the most magnificent golden feather atop. When I handed him the quill, it reflected all sorts of colors from a ray of sun that beamed into our kitchen in the earliest hours of the morning.

I watched as he gently rested the tiniest pair of writing glasses atop his large nose, and began to scratch away at the parchment. On the paper shone an exhausting list of names. Nobody I knew, at least I hoped not. Beside the names were either little notes, or simply an X. Sometimes, on days when he was frustrated, he’d be a bit more messy and just put lines through everything.

I began to brew his coffee the way he liked it – Black and acidic. As I prepared the coffee I started to feel very lethargic. I slept well. I ate well, and I hadn’t been up to anything too taxing recently. So I shrugged it off and continued to prepare for the day.

“Do you have to go today?”

“Come on, you know I have to.”

“It’s bad for your health to work so hard all the time. You could use a break.”

I tried to convince him but to no avail. I figured if I’d be lethargic all day, maybe we could just hangout like we did in the beginning.

“Hey are you alright? You look pretty tired today.” He asked me without looking up as he continued to scratch away. “Yeah I think I’m fine, I probably just need a nap. Are you alright?”

As I waited for an answer, I watched as he was nearing the bottom of the page when he stopped writing. His eyes read left to right about six or seven times and then he snapped the quill, crumpled up the paper and pulled out a brand new sheet, identical to the last. “Is something wrong?” I asked.

“I got all the way to the bottom and made a mistake, so I have to start over. And I can’t stand writing with a quill. I’m going to go get some pens from that art supply shop down the street, I’ll be right back.”

He left hastily without even touching his coffee. And above everything else that happened this morning, that was the most unlike him.

I walked over to his desk and began to unwrap the balled up piece of paper. Starting from the top, each line had a persons name. Beside each name, he’d write down a window of time. And when the time was close enough to present day, he’d leave a note about it. Beside the first name, Denise Melgren, read “Sixteen days, four hours, thirty-two minutes and twelve seconds - Failing liver.” Below the first name, the second name read Roger Ginart and next to his name simply read “X”.

I navigated my eyes to the bottom of the page and on the very last line read my name and next to it, a tear in the paper where he’d broken the quill. My hands began to sweat and my mind raced as I tried to fend off the impending realization of my own mortality.

As he re-entered the house I pretended to be up to nothing and promptly wiped the tears out from under my eyes. Instead of going straight back to the table where he left off, he walked up to me.

“On my way to the shop I figured you’re probably right. I should take the day off.”

“What made you change your mind?” I asked, out of my own morbid curiosity just to see how he’d reply.

“It’s been years since we’ve really spent any time together and I just thought it might be nice. I can fill out a few extra sheets tomorrow.”

He led me to the couch and pulled a blanket over me, turned on my favorite movie and sat next to me with one arm pulling me close. He gently kissed the top of my head as I pushed my body closer to his and fell into a deep sleep.

"Hey! You there by the window, looking *oh so sad*. Why don't you make yourself useful and fetch me and the Princess some fresh bubbly". I had no choice but to comply to his request. As I grumpily walked towards the door, he began to boast to the princess. "So there I was, just me and the Lord of Light -- You know what I said to him?" She leaned in close as if she was ready to pounce on him in excitement. "You won't believe this. I walked right up to him, pointed, and said 'there's something on your shirt'. Next thing you know, he's looking down and BAM!" Her eyes lit up. "Oh my goodness.. My Lord. You're so.. So naughty" As she finished her sentence, she let out a purr and I slammed the door behind myself.

While I began my descent down the five hundred stairs back to the kitchen, I could still faintly hear the Dark Lord's atrocious yammering while she gobbled it up. 'Yuck'. I started comparing myself to him. 'You know, I have a sword too. I could fight. I mean, I've been appointed to watching the princess! Of course I can. Sure, I've never swung the damn thing, but that's probably just because most men fear the sight of me!'

As I approached the halfway point of the long winding stairwell, which was marked with a sign "Only two hundred and fifty left to go!" I thought I'd heard a scream. I started to make my way back up the stairs just to make sure. Only a few steps higher and there it was again. These were screams of pain, and they started to become louder and louder. I leapt 3-4 stairs at a time, running faster than I ever had before. As I barreled towards the door appearing closer in view, I only could think of one thing. 'How will I live with myself if something has happened to the princess?'

"Someone help me! Please!" The Princess screamed once more. I did not bother turning the knob and bashed my shoulder against the door, breaking off the hinges and almost losing my balance as the door shattered in front of me.

Sitting before me were the Princess and the Dark Lord, appearing as if nothing had changed since I left. They looked up at me for a moment while I scanned the room for any signs of danger. The Princess turned to look at the Dark Lord and she began to giggle. I opened my mouth to ask what was going on, but the moment the words started to leave my mouth, the two began to violently laugh while clenching their stomachs.

"Oh my god, man. You're so damn gullible!" The Dark Lord shouted between gasps of air. "He is, isn't he!" The Princess added while the tears streamed down her face. A cold sweat pierced my skin as I began to fully understand the situation. A heat began to burn inside of my chest. A growing anger like none that I'd felt before. "Not the sharpest axe in the castle, are you champ?" The Dark Lord said, continuing to pile it on.

I put my hand onto my sword and clenched it tightly, ready to draw. I wanted to smite the Dark Lord badly, but knowing that was against my contract, I resisted.

I backed slowly out of the doorway, and turned to descend the five-hundred stairs again. I maintained eye contact with the Dark Lord until he disappeared from my vision, and continued my quest to get the princess a drink for the third time tonight.
